profile.name: Omik
profile.role: DevOps Engineer · Platform Automation & AI Systems
profile.headline: I automate server infrastructure with Terraform and Prometheus, train domain-specific AI models, and integrate autonomous agents directly into production.
profile.status: Available for Remote DevOps Roles, Terraform Stacks & AI Agent Deployments
profile.hero_lead: I design declarative cloud environments, automate server provisioning, and keep Linux services online without manual toil. Whether writing modular Terraform stacks, tuning Prometheus alert rules, fine-tuning open AI models on domain datasets, or deploying autonomous triage agents into production daemons — everything I build is deterministic, observable, and version-controlled.
about: No production system should depend on human memory or manual SSH sessions. When you configure a server by hand, you introduce undocumented drift that inevitably breaks during an outage. I treat infrastructure as software: every VPC, firewall rule, storage mount, and service container is declared in Terraform or SaltStack, tested against staging, and rolled out automatically.

Monitoring is useless if it creates alert fatigue. In my observability setups with Prometheus and Grafana, I focus strictly on actionable signals — saturation thresholds, error rate spikes, disk exhaustion curves, and latency percentiles. Alertmanager routes incidents directly to on-call channels with enough context to diagnose the issue in minutes rather than digging through blind logs.

Bridging DevOps and applied AI requires high engineering rigor. I curate domain datasets from logs and codebase histories to fine-tune open foundation models via LoRA, reducing hallucination. When running autonomous agents on production Linux nodes, they execute under locked-down systemd units and least-privilege service accounts, triaging healthchecks and drafting runbooks safely.

I prioritize lightweight, high-performance tooling across the entire stack. From Alpine-based minimal Docker containers with sub-second startup times to this very site pre-rendered as native static HTML via Rust, I build systems that are fast by default, lean on resource utilization, and trivial to recover when things break.

now.reading: eBPF tracepoints in the Linux 6.x kernel, low-overhead Prometheus metric scraping at scale, and dataset distillation techniques.
now.location_note: Bogura, Bangladesh (UTC+6) — collaborating with distributed engineering teams worldwide.

projects.title: Automated Multi-Node Cloud Platform with Terraform & Prometheus
projects.headline: Declarative Terraform HCL modules spinning up hardened Linux hosts, paired with automated Prometheus metric collectors and Alertmanager routing.
projects.problem: Setting up new servers was previously done via manual SSH sessions, forgotten firewall configurations, and inconsistent packages. When services degraded under load, the team only found out after customer complaints.
projects.solution: Wrote clean, modular Terraform configurations to provision VPS instances, private networking, and firewall rules in minutes. Automated the deployment of Prometheus and Node Exporter via cloud-init, streaming real-time system metrics to Grafana. Configured Alertmanager to notify on-call engineers within 15 seconds if disk I/O saturates or CPU throttles.

projects.title: Domain-Specific AI Model Training on Custom Engineering Datasets
projects.headline: Fine-tuning open weights on internal documentation and system logs for accurate, zero-hallucination technical assistance.
projects.problem: Generic foundation models routinely hallucinated proprietary API endpoints, outdated configuration parameters, and internal command syntax when queried by team members.
projects.solution: Curated and cleaned thousands of structured instruction-tuning pairs in JSONL format from internal technical documentation and commit histories. Fine-tuned an open-source model using parameter-efficient LoRA techniques, quantized the weights for fast inference, and wrapped the model in an asynchronous FastAPI service. Reduced technical hallucination to near zero on internal workflows.

projects.title: Production Server AI Agent with Automated Incident Triage
projects.headline: A background Python daemon connecting Alertmanager webhooks to an autonomous AI agent for instant failure diagnosis on live servers.
projects.problem: Waking up at 3 AM to SSH into servers, manually running dmesg, ss, and journalctl, and figuring out why a worker died costs valuable time during production outages.
projects.solution: Engineered an event-driven daemon running as a systemd service. When Prometheus fires an alert webhook, the agent safely executes non-destructive diagnostic commands over SSH, filters out sensitive data, analyzes the root cause, and posts an incident summary to Slack with the verified rollback or fix command ready for human sign-off.

projects.title: High-Availability E-Commerce & CMS Cloud Platform (wp-saltstack)
projects.headline: Fault-tolerant, auto-healing LAMP/LEMP platform orchestrated via wp-saltstack behind active-passive HAProxy and Nginx layer-7 ingress.
projects.problem: Monolithic e-commerce instances on single droplets suffered unmonitored crash loops, cascade failovers during sales surges, and configuration drift across servers.
projects.solution: Engineered reproducible infrastructure state using SaltStack (wp-saltstack formula) with automated state enforcement across Debian/Ubuntu nodes. Ingress terminates at dual HAProxy load balancers running keepalived for virtual IP failover, distributing traffic to horizontally scaled Nginx + PHP-FPM workers with automated Let's Encrypt TLS renewal and sub-180s recovery time.

projects.title: Server-Side Tracking & Ad-Ops Telemetry Pipeline
projects.headline: Custom server-side GTM proxy and event broker preserving conversion telemetry through Safari ITP and ad-blocker signal loss.
projects.problem: Client-side tracking scripts were losing up to 35% of ad attribution and revenue telemetry due to aggressive ad-blockers, iOS privacy sandboxing, and Safari cookie limits, distorting ROAS calculations.
projects.solution: Engineered a hardened Server-Side Google Tag Manager (sGTM) cluster hosted on a custom first-party subdomain behind Nginx with Redis event deduplication. Client events send raw HTTP data payloads directly to the server container, which enriches, normalizes, and dispatches server-to-server calls to Meta Conversions API (CAPI) and GA4 Measurement Protocol with 99.4% event match quality and zero client CPU overhead.
